text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said that it expected future provisions to total between about 400 Swiss francs and 600 million francs per year.
In November the group said it was taking a 1.4 billion franc provision for credit risks in 1996 to cover the weak part of its loan portfolio over the next two to three years.
The group took special provisions for credit risks of 3.0 billion franc in 1996 for the next two years.
This meant that a total amount of 4.4 billion in provisions for credit risks was charged to 1996 income.
"Thanks to UBS's forward-looking action against the loan impairment problem, future provisions should amount to between 400-600 million per year," UBS said in a statement presenting 1996 results.
